identity.industry: Downstream Steel Processing & High-Value Coated Products

summary.oneLiner: BMW Industries closed FY26 with record profitability driven by improved asset utilization, setting the stage for a transformational shift from a pure conversion model to an integrated buy-and-sell model via the Q1FY27 commissioning of the Bokaro greenfield project. The guided 75% revenue CAGR (FY25-FY28) reflects volume scaling and raw material inclusion rather than just organic growth, with margins expected to stabilize at 12-13% EBITDA as high-value ZAM and color-coated products ramp up.

one-line thesis: BMW Industries closed FY26 with record profitability driven by improved asset utilization, setting the stage for a transformational shift from a pure conversion model to an integrated buy-and-sell model via the Q1FY27 commissioning of the Bokaro greenfield project. The guided 75% revenue CAGR (FY25-FY28) reflects volume scaling and raw material inclusion rather than just organic growth, with margins expected to stabilize at 12-13% EBITDA as high-value ZAM and color-coated products ramp up.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 210 Cr (Q4), INR 665 Cr (FY26); EBITDA: INR 58 Cr (Q4, 27.5% margin), INR 165 Cr (FY26, 24.8% margin); PAT: INR 33 Cr (Q4, record), INR 81 Cr (FY26); Order Book: Not disclosed (short 2-week lead time, volatile raw materials); Net Debt: INR 364 Cr (0.45x D/E), includes INR 143 Cr for Bokaro; One-offs: Trade receivables spiked to INR 150 Cr due to timing delay from one key customer (paid in April), not credit deterioration.
guidance: Revenue CAGR ~75% (FY25-FY28); EBITDA CAGR ~45%; PAT CAGR ~40%; Stabilized EBITDA margin 12-13%, PAT margin 5-6% by FY28; Bokaro Phase 1 commissioning Q1FY27 (color coated first), meaningful sales Q2FY27.
order book & pipeline: No formal order book maintained due to short 2-week order-to-delivery cycle and raw material price volatility (zinc/aluminum); sales driven by spot/short-term contracts.
segment / subsidiary detail: CRM Complex production: ~718k MT (annualized utilization 70.9%); Pipes & Tubes production: 201k MT (up from 177k MT), current utilization ~34%, targeting 60-65% in 2-3 years; Bokaro Phase 1: Color coated (2 lakh tons capacity) starts Q1FY27, followed by Galvalume, Cold Rolling, Pickling.
growth verticals / optionality: ZAM (Zinc-Aluminum-Manganese) coated products offering 5-6x life vs standard galvanized, targeting solar/infra sectors with supply shortage; Export market expansion; Internal consumption of cold-rolled/galvanized feed for color coating to capture full value chain margins.
margins & cost dynamics: Current high margins (27.5% Q4) reflect pure conversion model; future blended margins (12-13%) reflect buy-and-sell model including raw material costs; spreads stable long-term despite short-term aberrations; raw material control via Bokaro reduces procurement costs and improves quality consistency.
capex / expansion: Total Bokaro project cost ~INR 803 Cr; INR 109 Cr funded via internal accruals in FY26; Remaining funded via debt (approx. 70-75%) and equity (25-30%); Peak debt expected INR 700-800 Cr within 12-15 months.
capital allocation: Subsidies (Jharkhand policy/PLI) to be used strictly for debt repayment per bank agreement; Final dividend INR 0.43/share (12% payout); Focus on deleveraging post-commissioning.
risks & watch-items: Raw material price volatility (zinc, aluminum) impacting hedging and margins; Execution risk on Bokaro ramp-up and quality stabilization; Delay in market acceptance of ZAM products; Working capital strain during ramp-up (target 30-40 days cycle).
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasizes 'sweating assets' and operational efficiency; Cautious on near-term quarterly guidance due to model transition; Transparent on accounting changes (capitalization of interest/depreciation phased with commissioning).
non-obvious takeaways: The 75% revenue CAGR is largely arithmetic due to the shift from 'conversion revenue' (net of material) to 'buy-and-sell revenue' (gross of material), not purely volume growth; ZAM product premium is marginal initially but value derives from customer lifecycle cost savings (solar 20-30 year guarantees); Receivable spike was purely timing, not credit risk.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply shortage of long-life coated steel for solar EPCs requiring 20-30 year guarantees | Waaree Energies | beneficiary | Med | Potential off-taker for ZAM products offering superior corrosion resistance for solar structures. |
| Need for high-strength, lightweight steel in automotive/infra to reduce weight | Tata Steel | beneficiary | Low | Peer in downstream but BMW's niche ZAM focus may capture specific premium segments Tata serves broadly. |
| Rising zinc prices making traditional galvanizing expensive for end-users | JSW Steel | beneficiary | Low | Upstream supplier potentially benefiting from increased demand for coated products if BMW scales ZAM adoption. |

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
